gap8.Receipt: verifyReceipt records actual worker output digests on frozen paths; legacy non-worker SHA is unchanged
gap8.RunCheck: durable authenticated checks claim; frozen declarations; host/Apple or native fixed SSH check observer
gap8.Advance: current commit/output/check binding, empty gaps and all-pass, then existing procedure gate
gap8.Return: shared session_handover.py producer, consume-before-redispatch and gaps in prompt without maxAttempts debit
gap8.Park: unknown intent, unavailable runner, zero/unknown counts, declaration/coverage failure, no-progress or ceiling
gap8.Linux: Gap8SSHChecks models pinned image+arming+log+teardown; live backend/image acceptance remains pending
gap8.OutputContract: Gap8OutputContract A; recorded Git bytes and TOCTOU checks; bounded receipt protocol, not an OS-wide host write jail

gap7.RunSkill: observeSpec: registry-resolved run-tlc.mjs availability check, pinned safe and unsafe runs, then private _spec admission
gap7.Confirm: optional committed chart pin matches bytes at revision; abstract confirmation covers the reviewed design bundle, not a generated adapter chart
gap7.EarlyPass: both-mode invariant-test commands pass at revision; g8-only timing satisfies this abstract condition vacuously
gap7.Dispatch: decide pre-act guard and transition dispatch specPassed guard; checked stack copied to intent
gap7.Edit: changed pinned bytes or workflow contract cannot reuse the previous manifest digest
gap7.CompleteGuard: safe exit zero with complete result, unsafe exit one naming mustViolate
gap7.DigestGuard: git show revision:path and pinned SHA-256 comparison
gap7.DeriveGuard: intent stack copied only from host-checked s.spec.derived
gap7.ConfirmGuard: declared chart must exist at revision
gap7.ChartGuard: declared chart SHA-256 equals confirmed manifest pin
gap7.EarlyCheckGuard: both-mode early invariant tests require success and positive observed test count

note: Expected runtime checks, not claims these tests already exist or that a model proves code

actions.RecordIntent: durable journal before any effect; per-step budget
actions.Effect: unique effect ID and effect-time epoch/writer; branch is a target receipt check outside this model
actions.JournalAck: reply journaled separately after the external effect
actions.Crash: abrupt exit before effect and after effect before acknowledgement
actions.Resume: ack selects a preferred recovery path; its guard checks conformance, not a proven-needed outcome fence; unknown effects never authorize resend
actions.ReconcileAbsent: trusted exact readback confirms no effect; retry only within budget
actions.ReconcilePresent: ack suppresses redundant present readback as a conformance rule; removing this check does not break a modeled outcome
actions.ReconcileOld: trusted terminal readback retires effect after release/transfer before new dispatch
actions.ReadbackWrong: unsafe control: false absent readback permits double effect
actions.ReceiveGood: independently checked result bound to dispatch ID, dispatch-time epoch/writer, step and commit
actions.ReceiveStale: old epoch receipt rejected even while parked
actions.ReceiveUnverified: unverified report cannot overwrite a trusted good result or advance
actions.ReceiveForgedCurrent: untrusted held result mislabeled current fails trusted dispatch-time admission
actions.ReceiveOldDispatch: old effect ID with otherwise plausible current labels fails the own-dispatch equality guard
actions.LateResult: late result after cancel stays observable but cannot advance
actions.ObserveTransition: unverified transition is a hint, not completion
actions.Wake: wake preserves verified result and cannot redispatch
actions.Release: owner release must reconcile old effect
actions.Transfer: writer match and transfer epoch bump cover for each other; removing both admits an old-writer advance
actions.Advance: checked trusted result, dispatch-time epoch/writer, exact effect ID and journal; terminal cancelled phase fences progress, while cancel epoch is defence in depth
actions.Cancel: terminal phase fences the stopped step; epoch bump is a conformance check and defence in depth, not an independently necessary modeled fence
